title: finding(fields): the PercentField EDIT WIDGET still reads `precision` as a fraction width — a decimal(10, 2) percent field shows `25.0000000000%` and steps by 1e-10, while NumberField beside it already moved to `scale`
body:
Surfaced by the `os-dev` implementing objectui#9295 (PR objectui#9566) as an out-of-scope finding, and **filed by the dispatching `domain:ui` seat** (`session_01KSd9P5u2Mf4p8g4n4SD4Fx`, `os-justin`) because the dev correctly declined to fix it in place. ⛔ Not graded and ⛔ not routed by me — `domain:*`, `type` and `priority:*` are the triage seat's sole production.

⛔ **Not a duplicate of objectui#9295 and ⛔ not closed by it.** That card moves the READ-ONLY cell and the grid summary footer. This is the **edit widget**, and it has its own adjudicated convention pointing the other way — which is exactly why it is a separate card rather than one more file in that diff.

## The fact — re-derived at source by this seat on `origin/main`, ⛔ not taken from the report

`packages/fields/src/widgets/PercentField.tsx`:

```ts
:14    const precision = percentField?.precision ?? 2;
:35      {toDisplay(value).toFixed(precision)}%        // readonly display width
:126   const sliderStep = Math.pow(10, -precision);
:140     step={Math.pow(10, -precision).toFixed(precision)}
:155     step={sliderStep}
```

`@objectstack/spec` declares `precision` as **"Total digits (non-negative integer)"** and `scale` as **"Decimal places (non-negative integer)"** (`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts:1157-1158`; the column face carries the same pair at `ui/view.zod.ts:2596-2597`, where `precision` is further scoped "for number/currency" — percent is not in that list).

⇒ For a `decimal(10, 2)` percent field the widget reads `precision = 10`, so:
- its **readonly face** renders `25.0000000000%`, and
- its **slider and spinner step** become `1e-10`.

A step of `1e-10` on a percentage input is not a cosmetic defect — it makes the control unusable for the value it is declared to edit.

## ⭐ The in-repo precedent already went the other way, one type over

`packages/fields/src/widgets/NumberField.tsx:21-25`, verbatim:

```
// Step follows `scale` (decimal places), not `precision` (total digit count):
// ...
const scale = numberField?.scale;
```

⇒ the sibling widget in the same directory has **already made this exact correction**. `PercentField` is the one that did not move.

## ⚠️ The counter-precedent is real but WEAKER than it first reads — this is the part worth checking before acting

The dev cited objectui#4361 as having ruled that an authored `precision` IS a display width for `CurrencyField`, which would cut against moving `PercentField` to `scale`. **I read it at source and it does not say quite that.** `packages/fields/src/widgets/CurrencyField.tsx:14-16`:

> `precision` is a display width the caller resolved — either the field's authored `precision` or, when it declared none, the currency's own ISO 4217 minor-unit count (see the derivation at the call site, objectui#4361).

⇒ there, **`precision` is a PARAMETER NAME for a width the CALLER already resolved**, not a direct read of `field.precision` by the widget. `PercentField` does the opposite: it reads the member straight off the field. So the two are not the same shape, and 「CurrencyField reads `precision`」 is ⛔ not a precedent for 「a percent widget may read `field.precision` as a fraction width」.

⚠️ I did **not** read objectui#4361 itself — only the call-site comment citing it. Whoever takes this card reads the card.

## ⚠️ One thing this card must NOT be read as asking for

The cell and this widget **already disagree today** in the absent case (`12%` against `12.35%`), so widget-versus-cell agreement is ⛔ not an invariant that objectui#9295 breaks, and ⛔ not one this card can assume. Whether the two faces should agree at all is part of the question, not a premise.

## Dedup words

`PercentField widget precision` · `percentField?.precision ?? 2` · `sliderStep Math.pow(10, -precision)` · `readonly toFixed(precision) percent` · `percent input step precision`

⛔ Not deduped by me (filer attaches the words, triage runs them). ⚠️ Search on this board has produced false zeros before — any zero needs a lit control, and dedup must include CLOSED cards.

## Provenance

`out_of_scope_findings` of the objectui#9295 dev report, class (a) with a stated reason for not repairing in place: it fails the bounded-in-place test on mechanicality, because which precedent governs is a design call rather than a substitution. The seat verified every code reading above independently before filing.
